io.name: rst

io.notes: Freeze control for the ID stage.

io.name: ex_freeze
io.notes: Freeze control for the EX stage.

io.name: wb_freeze
io.notes: Freeze control for the WB stage.

io.name: flushpipe
io.notes: Pipeline flush request.

io.name: if_insn

io.name: ex_insn
io.notes: EX-stage instruction register.

io.name: branch_op

io.name: branch_taken
io.notes: Current branch decision used for delay-slot control.

io.name: rf_addra

io.name: rf_addrb
io.notes: Source-B register address, directly from if_insn[15:11].

io.name: rf_rda

io.name: rf_rdb
io.notes: Source-B register-read indicator, from if_insn[30].

io.name: alu_op

io.name: mac_op

io.name: shrot_op

io.name: comp_op

io.name: rf_addrw
io.notes: EX-control-time register-file write destination.

io.name: rfwb_op
io.notes: Registered EX-stage write-back selector and validity encoding.

io.name: wb_insn

io.name: simm

io.name: branch_addrofs

io.name: lsu_addrofs

io.name: sel_a

io.name: sel_b

io.name: lsu_op

io.name: cust5_op

io.name: cust5_limm

io.name: multicycle

io.name: spr_addrimm

io.name: wbforw_valid

io.name: du_hwbkpt

io.name: sig_trap

io.name: force_dslot_fetch

io.name: no_more_dslot

io.name: ex_void

io.name: ex_macrc_op
io.notes: Registered EX-stage MAC-result-read indication.

io.name: rfe

io.name: except_illegal

ex_insn.notes: An accepted instruction advances through ID into EX on the next advancing posedge; ex_freeze holds EX.

branch_op.notes: Registered from ID-stage branch predecode on a posedge; a flush or ID bubble produces an inactive operation.

alu_op.notes: Registered with EX control from the ID-stage instruction on a posedge.

mac_op.notes: Registered with EX control; inactive when MAC support is disabled.

rf_addrw.notes: Updated at the EX-control posedge from the ID-stage instruction; it is not necessarily cleared by flushpipe.

wb_insn.notes: Updated from ex_insn on the next advancing posedge; wb_freeze holds WB.

simm.notes: Combinational from the current ID-stage instruction; aligned one stage after the accepted if_insn.

branch_addrofs.notes: Combinational from ex_insn and aligned with the EX instruction. The output is [31:2] and receives no additional shift.

lsu_addrofs.notes: Combinational from ex_insn and aligned with the EX instruction.

sel_a.notes: Combinational from the current ID instruction and forwarding state.

sel_b.notes: Combinational from the current ID instruction and forwarding state; immediate selection has priority.

cust5_op.notes: Combinational from ex_insn and therefore aligned with EX.

cust5_limm.notes: Combinational from ex_insn and therefore aligned with EX.

multicycle.notes: Combinationally decoded from the current ID instruction.

spr_addrimm.notes: Registered with EX control; cleared for a bubble or flush.

sig_trap.notes: Trap decode and du_hwbkpt are sampled into EX-stage trap control on a posedge.

no_more_dslot.notes: Combinational from current branch control, ID void status, and branch_taken.

id_macrc_op.notes: Combinationally decoded from the current ID instruction.

ex_macrc_op.notes: Registered version of the ID MAC-result-read decode.

rfe.notes: Asserted from either early branch predecode or registered EX branch control.

functional_summary: The module contains ID, EX, and WB instruction pipeline registers. if_insn advances into ID, ID advances into EX, and EX advances into WB on rising clock edges subject to reset, flush, and stage freezes.

rst is active-high asynchronous reset. Reset has priority over flush and freezes and sets instruction pipeline registers to the OR1200 void or NOP encoding 32'h0001_0000, with registered controls set inactive.

flushpipe forces the ID, EX, and WB instruction registers to the OR1200 void or NOP encoding and clears the EX-stage functional controls specified by the implementation. It does not implicitly clear every internal register; rf_addrw, WB destination tracking, and sel_imm retain their specified register behavior unless updated by their own logic.

When id_freeze is asserted while ex_freeze is deasserted, the held ID instruction is not re-executed: EX receives the void or NOP instruction and inactive controls. ex_freeze holds EX and wb_freeze holds WB.
rf_addra equals if_insn[20:16], rf_addrb equals if_insn[15:11], rf_rda equals if_insn[31], and rf_rdb equals if_insn[30].

ID decode produces simm, sel_a, sel_b, multicycle, sel_imm, immediate-extension control, and id_macrc_op. EX control registration produces alu_op, mac_op, shrot_op, comp_op, lsu_op, branch_op, rfwb_op, spr_addrimm, sig_syscall, sig_trap, ex_macrc_op, and except_illegal.

Forwarding selection defaults to the register file. For each source, EX forwarding has priority over valid WB forwarding. Register zero does not create a forwarding dependency. Source-use indicators gate forwarding comparisons. For sel_b, immediate selection has priority over forwarding.

simm expands id_insn[15:0]. Sign extension is used for addi, addic, xori, enabled muli or maci, and immediate compare instructions. Other immediate forms use zero extension according to the OR1200 decode.

branch_addrofs is the 30-bit output corresponding to sign extension of ex_insn[25:0] into bits [31:2]. No additional shift is applied. lsu_addrofs uses sign-extended {ex_insn[25:21],ex_insn[10:0]} for stores and sign-extended {ex_insn[15:11],ex_insn[10:0]} for loads and default cases.

rf_addrw normally uses id_insn[25:21]. When pre_branch_op identifies JR or BAL, rf_addrw is forced to register r9. Actual write-back remains controlled by rfwb_op; JAL and JALR generate link-register write-back, while ordinary J and JR do not.

spr_addrimm uses id_insn[15:0] for l.mfspr and {id_insn[25:21],id_insn[10:0]} for other applicable SPR operations, including l.mtspr. It resets to zero and is cleared when EX receives a bubble or the pipeline is flushed.

multicycle uses id_insn[9:8] for OR1200_OR32_ALU and otherwise uses OR1200_ONE_CYCLE. Load/store multi-cycle cases inside an UNUSED conditional block are inactive unless that block is explicitly enabled.
shrot_op is derived from id_insn[7:6], comp_op is derived from id_insn[24:21], and lsu_op selects load/store size and sign behavior while defaulting inactive for non-memory instructions.
When MAC support is enabled, mac_op and MAC-result-read decode support the implemented MAC instructions. When MAC support is disabled, mac_op, id_macrc_op, and ex_macrc_op are inactive.

pre_branch_op identifies branch, jump, jump-register, branch-if-flag, branch-if-no-flag, and RFE operations. branch_op is the registered EX-stage form. rfe asserts when either early predecode or EX branch control identifies RFE.
no_more_dslot asserts when a branch operation is present, the ID instruction is not void, and branch_taken is true, or when the current branch operation is RFE. force_dslot_fetch is hardwired to 0.

except_illegal is asserted for unrecognized or unsupported encodings and is cleared for supported encodings. Legal instruction coverage depends on the compile-time MAC, multiplication, and custom-instruction feature configuration. sig_syscall detects l.sys; sig_trap detects l.trap or du_hwbkpt.
cust5_op and cust5_limm are direct EX-instruction subfields. Custom instruction legality and ALU selection are enabled only when the corresponding compile-time support is enabled.
corner_cases: Reset is asynchronous and active high. Asserted rst immediately establishes the reset values; registered outputs are checked after reset assertion and after the following rising edge.
Reset has priority over flushpipe and all freeze controls.
flushpipe has priority over normal stage advancement and forces id_insn, ex_insn, and wb_insn to 32'h0001_0000. EX functional controls and spr_addrimm are inactive or zero as specified.
Registers without explicit flush handling, including rf_addrw, WB destination tracking, and sel_imm, are not assumed to clear solely because flushpipe is asserted.

If id_freeze and ex_freeze are both asserted, EX holds its current contents because ex_freeze controls EX. If id_freeze is asserted and ex_freeze is deasserted, EX receives a bubble rather than the held ID instruction.
A void or NOP instruction is not illegal and must not request register write-back, memory operation, branch action, syscall, or trap.
The void or NOP encoding is 32'h0001_0000, and bit 16 is set for void detection. ex_void detects this encoding from ex_insn.
branch_addrofs has width 30 and represents [31:2]. It is sign-extended from the 26-bit ex_insn[25:0] field without an additional shift.
Immediate and offset arithmetic uses explicit fixed-width extensions and wraps modulo 2^32 where a 32-bit result is required.
For simultaneous EX and WB forwarding matches, EX forwarding wins. WB forwarding requires wbforw_valid and a valid WB write-back indication. Register zero never causes forwarding.
sel_b immediate selection overrides both EX and WB forwarding selections.
du_hwbkpt contributes to the registered EX-stage sig_trap indication and does not modify pipeline instruction contents.
Feature-dependent MAC, multiplication, and custom instruction behavior is determined at compile time. Unsupported instructions must default to safe inactive controls and except_illegal asserted.
force_dslot_fetch is always 0, including during reset, flush, branches, and freezes.
test_plan: Assert rst asynchronously and verify the void or NOP instruction value and inactive registered controls. Deassert rst and verify normal operation on rising clock edges.
Drive distinct instructions before successive rising edges and verify ID-to-EX and EX-to-WB movement with one-cycle stage latency.
Verify that all sequential outputs are checked after the rising edge that updates them, with no half-cycle sampling or edge-based latency interpretation.
Verify rf_addra, rf_addrb, rf_rda, and rf_rdb directly for varied if_insn values, including all-zero and all-one words.

Exercise id_freeze, ex_freeze, and wb_freeze independently and in combinations. Specifically verify bubble insertion when ID is frozen while EX advances, EX hold when ex_freeze is asserted, and WB hold when wb_freeze is asserted.

Assert flushpipe during each freeze combination and verify void or NOP instruction values and inactive EX controls while checking that registers without explicit flush handling retain their contracted behavior.
Test immediate sign-extension and zero-extension classes with values 0x0000, 0x7fff, 0x8000, and 0xffff.
Test load and store split offsets and branch offset sign boundaries, including positive and negative values.
Test forwarding with no match, EX match, WB match, simultaneous EX and WB match, invalid wbforw_valid, register-zero destinations, and source-read-disabled cases. Verify immediate sel_b priority.
Exercise ordinary branches, jumps, JR, BAL, JAL, JALR, taken and not-taken decisions, RFE, and void ID instructions. Verify branch_op, rf_addrw, rfwb_op, no_more_dslot, and rfe.
Exercise legal and unsupported ALU, LSU, SFXX, SYS, TRAP, SPR, custom, multiply, and MAC encodings under each configured feature set.
Verify sig_syscall for l.sys, sig_trap for l.trap, sig_trap contribution from du_hwbkpt, illegal-instruction defaults, MAC-result-read timing, and constant force_dslot_fetch equal to 0.

verifier: Use the exact declared port names and widths and compile the same feature macros as the DUT; no module parameters exist.

Drive all inputs before each rising edge. Observe sequential outputs after the same rising edge has completed its nonblocking assignments, and perform all latency accounting in whole rising-edge cycles. Do not use an opposite-edge observation scheme. Use stage-aware queues: an accepted if_insn reaches EX after one advancing cycle, and wb_insn updates from ex_insn after one advancing cycle unless WB is frozen.

Model asynchronous reset independently of the clock and give reset priority over flushpipe and freezes. Check direct combinational outputs when their source inputs change, and check ID- and EX-aligned combinational outputs after the rising edge that updates the corresponding pipeline register.

Use procedural checks or simple immediate assertions compatible with Verilator rather than advanced SVA. Compare operation fields against the OR1200 decode constants compiled for the selected feature configuration.
coder: Match the exact interface and use sequential logic sensitive to posedge clk and posedge rst, with explicit reset values and reset, flush, and freeze priority.
Keep separate ID, EX, and WB instruction/state registers. Implement the id_freeze and advancing EX case as bubble insertion, and do not re-execute stale ID decode information.
Preserve the specified behavior of registers without explicit flush branches, including rf_addrw, WB destination tracking, and sel_imm.

Use explicit signed extensions and intermediate widths for 16-bit immediates, split LSU fields, and the 26-bit branch offset. Implement branch_addrofs as a 30-bit [31:2] signal without an implicit shift.
Centralize OR1200 opcode and selector constants, feature-gate MAC, multiplication, and custom decode, and default every decode path to safe inactive or NOP values.
Avoid multiple procedural and continuous drivers for any output.

Implement forwarding priority as immediate for sel_b, then EX forwarding, then valid WB forwarding, then register file. Gate comparisons with source-use, nonzero destination, and valid write-back conditions.
Ensure all sequential state is updated only on rising clock edges and that no design behavior depends on an opposite clock edge.
debugger: First check asynchronous reset sensitivity, reset priority, flush and freeze priority, and whole-cycle stage alignment at rising clock edges.
Check whether ID freeze incorrectly holds or re-executes an instruction instead of injecting an EX bubble, and whether EX or WB freezes overwrite held state.
Check the 32'h0001_0000 void or NOP encoding and bit-16 void detection after reset and flush.
Check signed versus zero extension, split store versus load offset fields, branch offset width [31:2], and accidental shifts or truncation.
Check forwarding priority, register-zero suppression, wbforw_valid gating, source-use gating, and sel_b immediate precedence.
Check feature-macro guards and default illegal behavior, then inspect link-register destination versus rfwb_op validity and du_hwbkpt trap timing.
If a latency mismatch is reported, trace values only across successive rising clock edges and verify that the checker is not introducing half-cycle sampling or an extra transaction delay.
